label: D1 after unrewarded S2 visit, growing steeply after trial ~60; quenched by two misses in a row
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 60, 0, None)**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 60, 0, None) ;; (phase == D1) * (1 - (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0)) * np.clip(ep_trial - 60, 0, None) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 60, 0, None)**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_common == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 60, 0, None) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * np.clip(ep_trial - 60, 0, None)
explanation: Fires only at D1, late in the episode. Magnitude grows about quadratically with trials past ~60 when the previous trial reached S2 and went unrewarded. It is near zero after any rewarded trial or any S1 visit (a negative late-ramp term on those D1 steps cancels the timing baseline). Within S2-unrewarded cases it is lower when the transition was rare (a1 -> S2) and much lower when the trial before was also unrewarded, so it peaks on the first miss at S2 after a reward. On the window first trial (previous state unknown, unrewarded) a smaller quadratic ramp covers the cases where S2 cannot be checked. Value/policy and the hidden good state add nothing. All terms are observed. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.66, against an additive-table ceiling of 0.15 (the ceiling misses the reward x state x episode-time interaction).

issues: The consecutive-miss term uses tv("reward", -2). On the window's second trial that value is outside the window, so the term is lost there, even though the same quantity can be observed as tv("prev_reward", -1) (the reward input at the previous D1). Swapping in tv("prev_reward", -1) raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.660 to 0.708 with the same 6 terms. Adding a quadratic version of the consecutive-miss term and a linear first-trial term brings it to 0.713. Example: the worst-fit window starting at t96 predicts 1.34 at t97, but the actual value is 0 after two misses in a row.

The claim that S2-unrewarded activation is lower after a rare transition is directionally right (weight -0.004), but the effect is tiny. Dropping the term moves test R^2 only from 0.660 to 0.657, so it should not be stated as a major factor.
The consecutive-miss quenching is the main modifier and holds up: without it test R^2 falls from 0.66 to 0.52.

The first-trial term (prev_state == -1) is a weak stand-in: window-first D1 steps are badly under-predicted (actual about 2.1, predicted 0.28 to 0.49). Nothing in the window can fix this, so it limits the fit rather than undermining the label.

The peaks of first misses are under-predicted by about half (for example 2.45 actual vs 1.29 predicted at t96). Extras within 8 terms add only 0.005 to 0.02 each: value, |choice|, good state, the state two trials back, three misses in a row, a reward streak. No large systematic class remains. Mean error is at most 0.006 in every phase and previous-trial cell.
Ramp onset barely matters: start at 50 gives 0.705, 60 gives 0.713, 70 gives 0.715, and an exponential ramp gives 0.691. 'Past about 60' is fine.
